title: Court-Appointed Monitor: California City ICE Facility Noncompliant in All 8 Medical Care Areas
excerpt: A federal court-appointed medical monitor found California's largest ICE detention facility failed to provide adequate healthcare in all eight assessed areas, violating a court order, and that untrained staff were being used to train new hires due to staffing shortages.
content:
On July 28, 2026, a court-appointed independent medical monitor released a damning report on the California City Immigration Processing Center, California's largest ICE detention facility, operated by private prison company CoreCivic.

  • Dr. Muthusamy Anandkumar found the facility was noncompliant in all eight assessed areas of medical care, concluding it "lacks a reliable system to consistently provide adequate healthcare, placing individuals at serious risk of both immediate and long-term harm."
  • The monitor found the facility lacked adequate staffing, stable on-site management, sufficient clinical oversight, or an effective quality assurance process. Staff had been "pulled from orientation before completing it … because of staffing shortages" — and employees who had not finished their own training were, in turn, training new hires.
  • Thirteen specific deficiencies were identified, including inadequate emergency response, insufficient dental care, poor management of chronic illnesses, missing prescribed medications, and monthslong delays in cancer treatment.
  • The report marked the first time a court-appointed neutral party had investigated the full scope of medical care delivery at an ICE detention facility, according to the ACLU.

The monitor's findings confirmed ICE was in violation of a February 2026 federal court order requiring adequate medical care at the facility. The report was based on a three-day site inspection, interviews with over a dozen staff and 40 patients, and reviews of 141 patient medical records.
